short_description: Enveloped herpesvirus (human alphaherpesvirus 3 / HHV-3; Orthoherpesviridae, subfamily Alphaherpesvirinae, genus Varicellovirus), ~180-200 nm and pleomorphic rather than perfectly spherical, built to the classic FOUR-LAYER herpesvirus plan: a single linear double-stranded DNA genome of 124,884 bp with ~71 ORFs - the smallest of the human herpesvirus genomes - packaged under pressure into a T=16 icosahedral capsid of 162 capsomeres (150 hexons + 12 pentons, ~100 nm nucleocapsid), that capsid cushioned by the tegument, an amorphous granular/fibrous protein layer that is the herpesvirus signature and is usually the layer illustrations omit, and the whole assembly wrapped in a host-derived lipid envelope carrying short (~8 nm) blunt glycoprotein spikes (gB, gC, gE/gI, gH/gL, gK, gM/gN). Primary airborne respiratory infection causes chickenpox; the virus then establishes lifelong latency in the neurons of dorsal-root, cranial-nerve and autonomic ganglia and can reactivate decades later, travelling back down a single nerve as dermatomal herpes zoster (shingles).

colour_legend.genome: coppery gold, tightly wound/spooled dsDNA filling the capsid interior
colour_legend.capsid: cool pale grey-blue icosahedral shell with discrete capsomere facets clearly faceted, not smooth
colour_legend.tegument: warm amber/tan GRANULAR padding filling real volume between capsid and envelope - a substantial textured zone, NOT a thin line and NOT a second membrane; drawn asymmetric so the capsid sits slightly off-centre
colour_legend.envelope: soft translucent lilac-grey lipid bilayer with a slightly irregular, scalloped outline (never a precise circle)
colour_legend.glycoprotein_spikes: short blunt rose/pink studs densely dotting the envelope surface - stubby, wider than long, never long or rod-like
colour_legend.background: neutral dark charcoal (watercolour: warm aged cream paper)
colour_legend.note: A virion has no pigment of its own; electron micrographs - including the real CDC PHIL #1878 TEM used as this microbe's reference - image in greyscale, so every colour here is teaching convention (see reference/colors.md). Keep this same structure->colour mapping across sem/textbook/3d/watercolor so the set reads as one poster.

do_not_draw: a naked capsid with no envelope - VZV is ALWAYS enveloped, unlike rotavirus and norovirus already in this atlas, which are non-enveloped
a smooth envelope with NO tegument between capsid and envelope - the tegument must read as a visible granular/fibrous layer filling real volume, never a thin membrane line or an empty gap
the tegument drawn as a second smooth membrane or lipid bilayer (it is amorphous/fibrous protein padding, not a membrane)
a perfectly spherical, geometrically precise particle - the envelope is pleomorphic, slightly irregular and scalloped in outline
a helical, rod-shaped, filamentous or bullet-shaped capsid, or a bacteriophage head-and-tail body with tail fibres, collar or base plate
long stalked club- or mushroom-headed spikes, a corona of clubs, or a fuzzy fringe (that is coronavirus/influenza) - VZV's glycoprotein spikes are SHORT (~8 nm), blunt and densely packed
RNA of any kind, a segmented genome, or a free B-form double helix with drawn base-pair rungs outside the capsid - the genome is ONE linear double-stranded DNA molecule, spooled inside the capsid
bacterial features of any kind: cell wall, peptidoglycan, flagellum, pilus, capsule, nucleoid, ribosomes - a virion is not a cell
a nucleus, mitochondria, cytoplasm or any other cell organelle
blisters, pustules, a rash, scratched skin or a distressed person in the four science styles (sem/textbook/3d/watercolor) - those are clinical signs of the disease, not virus morphology
a face, eyes, mouth or any anthropomorphism in the four science styles (reserved for the separate kids' coloring page)
more than one virion - a single specimen only, no duplicates
any baked-in text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars, rulers, legends or watermarks
a black border, dark frame, vignette, letterbox bar, mat, drop shadow, or the artwork drawn as a sheet/card lying on a surface

sources.claim: Four concentric layers (core/genome, icosahedral capsid, tegument, envelope); nucleocapsid ~100 nm of 162 capsomeres with 2-/3-/5-fold icosahedral symmetry; capsomeres are hollow hexagonal and pentagonal units; enveloped virion ~180-200 nm; envelope glycoprotein spikes ~8 nm long; nine glycoproteins gK, gN, gC, gB, gH, gM, gL, gI, gE forming gE-gI and gH-gL heterodimers; tegument an amorphous layer of loosely associated proteins including IE62 (major transactivator, ICP4 homolog) and IE63.
sources.source: ScienceDirect Topics, "Varicella Zoster Virus - an overview"

sources.claim: T=16 icosahedral symmetry; enveloped particle spherical to pleomorphic, 150-200 nm; genus Varicellovirus taxonomy.
Genome is a single linear duplex DNA molecule of 124,884 bp with at least 70 (71 unique) ORFs - the smallest alphaherpesvirus genome.
sources.source: ScienceDirect Topics VZV overview; concordant with NCBI RefSeq NC_001348 (Human alphaherpesvirus 3, Dumas strain).

sources.claim: Tegument proteins IE62/IE63 essential for replication; gE essential and most abundant, gE-gI governs cell-to-cell spread; gE is the antigen of the recombinant zoster subunit vaccine.
sources.source: Frontiers in Immunology (2020), "Manipulation of the Innate Immune Response by Varicella Zoster Virus"

sources.claim: The real TEM reference visually corroborates the four-layer architecture: a single isolated virion showing a lighter rounded capsid core, a dark granular tegument shell around it, and an irregular, scalloped outer envelope edge.
sources.source: Direct visual inspection of the downloaded CDC PHIL #1878 plate at native 1580 x 1911 px (see reference block).

reference.verified: Verified by direct download: HTTP 200, content-type image/tiff, 3,204,474 bytes. NOTE: despite the .tif extension the payload is actually a PNG, which Pillow decodes cleanly at 1580 x 1911 px, RGBA. The 700 x 846 px '_lores.jpg' variant of the same frame also returns HTTP 200 (85,415 bytes) - it must NOT be used as if it were the full-resolution file, and an earlier pass of this pipeline had wrongly fetched it, which would have meant a 1.54x UPSCALE to the 1080 canvas.
reference.content_check: PASS. A SINGLE, well-isolated VZV virion fills the middle of the frame - the ideal case the rubric asks for, not a clump. All three visible layers of the four-layer architecture read clearly: an irregular, scalloped OUTER ENVELOPE edge with a pronounced fold at the upper left (textbook pleomorphism, not a circle); a broad, dark, strongly GRANULAR tegument zone occupying most of the particle's area; and a lighter, rounded CAPSID sitting distinctly OFF-CENTRE within it (the characteristic tegument asymmetry). No baked-in text, no scale bar, no instrument data, no border.
reference.processing: The displayed reference is 'real-02__TEM-crop': a purely DETERMINISTIC crop with NO generative editing at all - a 1400 x 1400 px region taken at (25, 335) of the native 1580 x 1911 px file, Lanczos-resampled to 1080 x 1080. That is a 0.77x DOWNSCALE, so no pixels were invented and no shapes altered. edit_image.py was deliberately NOT run: the plate carries no text, no scale bar and no border, so there was nothing to clean, and an AI pass risked re-illustrating the negative-stain grain (exactly the failure that had to be reverted for rotavirus). The greyscale was left untouched - no false colour applied. The full centre-cropped frame is kept as 'real-01__TEM' for provenance.
